guide: This is a way to find the simple, boring faults in an app you are building before your users do, using an AI coding assistant and a few real testers. You need an app you are building, an AI coding assistant (ChatGPT / Codex or Claude Code), and one or two people willing to test it.
1. List the basic things every user needs to work first, such as sign-up, log-in, forgotten password, log-out and delete account.
1. Ask a friend or two to use the app as a new user and write down every point where something breaks or confuses them.
1. Test those same flows yourself on a real phone, using a fresh account rather than your developer one.
1. Paste each problem, with the exact error or what the tester saw, into ChatGPT (Codex) or Claude Code and ask it to find the cause in your code.
1. Fix one problem at a time and re-run the whole flow, including the email that arrives when someone resets a password.
1. Turn each fixed flow into a short written checklist, or an automated test, so it is checked before every release.
1. Only start on bigger or more exciting features once the whole checklist passes.
Watch out: Building the hard, interesting parts first is tempting, but a broken password reset or sign-up loses users before they see any of it.
